items.headline: US to blacklist Asian AI firm Megaspeed after Nvidia scandal
items.blurb: Megaspeed has been accused of funneling AI chips to China after a former executive's affair with Jensen Huang became public.
items.text: The US has said it intends to ban a Singaporean artificial intelligence (AI) company allegedly tied to the Nvidia scandal from doing business in America. The Department of Commerce announced it planned to add Megaspeed Ltd to a list of entities that are blacklisted from buying or selling goods in the US. The company is mainly a developer of data centres, but in recent weeks a former executive of Megaspeed was accused of working as spy for China while having a romantic relationship with Nvidia head Jensen Huang. The relationship led to additional scrutiny by US officials and heightened concern that Megaspeed was funnelling Nvidia's advanced AI computer chips to China. When exactly the ban against Megaspeed will go into effect was not specified in the commerce department announcement. The BBC has asked the agency for comment, along with the White House and Megaspeed. Megaspeed was not well known within the US until last month when media reports emerged that a former Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had an affair with Jensen Huang. items.text: An explosion on a Russian ship docked at Benghazi naval base was caused by a suspected drone attack, Libya's eastern government has said. The explosion happened at dawn on Sunday, while the ship had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way back to Russia, Libya state media reported, citing the eastern government. The statement said there were no casualties. Moscow has yet to comment. Later on Sunday, the health ministry said it had received injured people from another vessel, a commercial ship, that was also targeted off the coast of Benghazi, state media reported. Their injuries were minor and their condition stable, the ministry said. Videos posted on social media and geolocated by BBC Verify show the ship that was struck in the morning engulfed in flames and smoke. items.headline: Appeals court renews Trump bid for federal jurisdiction in hush-money case
items.blurb: The ruling could clear the way for Trump to argue prosecutors relied on evidence protected by presidential immunity.
items.text: A federal appeals court has revived United States President Donald Trump’s bid to transfer his New York criminal hush-money case to federal court, months after a district judge rejected the effort for a third time. On Monday, a three-judge panel of the 2nd Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court ruling that had kept the case in New York state court. In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein’s denial of Trump’s request for the “removal” of his case to federal court. The appeals court said Hellerstein had “erred in holding that removal is categorically unavailable in a state criminal case” after conviction. It directed a federal judge in Manhattan to consider whether the proceedings could be brought under federal jurisdiction. In a written statement provided to The Associated Press news agency, a spokesperson for Trump’s legal team said the president “appreciates the 2nd Circuit’s prompt and correct ruling, as he continues to win against Democrat weaponization of our Justice System”. items.text: No one has claimed responsibility for the strike on the vessel, which had docked on its way back to Russia A Russian warship docked in the Libyan port city of Benghazi was struck in the early hours of Sunday in a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack, causing a dramatic night-time explosion and the sinking of the vessel. The strike severely damaged the Merkury, a Russian navy corvette that had stopped to refuel and take on supplies, according to Libyan officials from the country’s eastern government. Initial reports said several Ukrainian sea drones were launched at the ship. At least four drones were intercepted and destroyed, while two hit the warship, triggering the explosion, the officials told the Associated Press. Satellite imagery showed the Merkury had sunk after the attack, which took place in the Mediterranean, more than 1,000 miles from south Ukraine , marking a notable geographic expansion of the now near five-year war. items.headline: What strike on Russian ship in Libya says about spread of Ukraine war
items.blurb: Ukraine's sinking of a Russian battleship at a port in Libya raises the stakes of the war a notch, writes Frank Gardner.
items.text: Anchored in a Mediterranean harbour nearly 2,000 miles from Moscow, the Captain of Russia's corvette Merkury might well have thought his ship was safe from attack. It wasn't. The audacious and successful night-time attack in Benghazi , co-ordinated by Ukraine's SBU intelligence agency and its armed forces, has raised the obvious question: is the Ukraine war spreading well beyond its borders? The answer is yes, in fact, it was already spreading. But this attack, which Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky called "an exemplary operation" will inevitably raise the stakes another notch. Russia, which is currently engaged in a non-stop campaign to batter Ukraine's civilian population into submission with daily missile and drone strikes , has called it "a dangerous escalation". It follows the suspected Ukrainian drone attack on a Russian dry-cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland at the weekend, which the Kremlin described as an act of terrorism. Ukraine's long-range drones have also previously struck Russia's Baltic oil terminal at Ust-Luga. items.headline: Israeli minister approves return of Flydubai flights
items.blurb: Final resumption of carrier's route between Dubai and Tel Aviv depends on Israeli security authorities' approval.
items.text: Israeli Transportation Minister Miri Regev has approved the resumption of Flydubai flights to Tel Aviv, according to Israeli media, almost two months after an onboard incident where a co-pilot was accused of attacking his captain. Regev made the announcement on Monday, though Israel’s security authorities’ approval is still required for flights to resume. The ministry expects operations to resume within a week or two, Israeli media said. The minister’s approval comes after talks between Israeli officials, led by ministry Director-General Moshe Ben-Zaken, and Emirati aviation officials took place in Dubai on November 16. Authorities discussed potential security measures that would allow for airlines to fully resume flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv. “The delegation today presented Regev with the steps the company has taken in the wake of the incident,” Israeli media reported, citing a transportation ministry statement. “As a result, Regev approved the return of Flydubai, subject to clearance from security authorities.” “The move is a significant step toward restoring air connectivity between Israel and the UAE and expanding flight options for passengers,” the statement added. items.text: Hazard warnings issued throughout week after powerful swells and waves of more than 9 metres recorded Multiple coastal hazard warnings were issued this week across California as successive areas of low pressure generated powerful swells and large breaking waves for coastal communities. Beaches and piers were closed last weekend as large waves crashed into California’s coastline. Offshore National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration buoys recorded wave heights of greater than 30ft (9 metres) last Friday. The Monterey, California, buoy recorded a wave height of 34.1ft, which would make it the highest reading in 30 years. Coastal warnings extended from last weekend through this week, with alerts extending until Friday night. Waves of 10–18ft are expected, with local sets of 18–22ft for San Luis Obispo county beaches and Santa Barbara county central coast beaches. These Pacific storm systems are also bringing unsettled conditions across the western US, with heavy rain, mountain snow, and strong winds through the coming days. items.headline: Iranian authorities flog singer who performed without hijab, lawyers say
items.blurb: Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were reportedly given 74 lashes in Qom.
items.text: A prominent singer who performed without the mandatory hijab and four members of her band and production team have been flogged by Iranian authorities, lawyers say. Parastoo Ahmadi, three musicians and a producer were each given 74 lashes in the city of Qom, a member of their defence team told the BBC. Ahmadi, 29, wore a sleeveless dress during a concert that was livestreamed in December 2024. Iran's laws ban public performances by women and require them to wear headscarves and modest clothing. This June, a criminal court in Qom convicted Ahmadi and eight others of "offending public decency" through the publication of "obscene and indecent material", which they had denied. In addition to being sentenced to 74 lashes, they were banned from audiovisual activities and from leaving the country for two years. At the end of September, an appeals court in Qom rejected the defendants' appeal and confirmed the sentence, her lawyers said. items.text: A 31-year-old software engineer has been arrested for allegedly murdering his 26-year-old friend, Komal Dahale, following an argument at her paying guest (PG) accommodation in Pune 's Hinjewadi area in the early hours of Monday. Dahale, a native of Wardha district in Maharashtra's Vidarbha region, was allegedly assaulted by the accused, Shubham Kalbande, during a dispute at her accommodation in Sakhare Vasti, police said. Both Dahale and Kalbande worked as software engineers at two major IT companies in Pune and had known each other for around three-and-a-half years. They were reportedly in a relationship and had been having frequent arguments over the past two to three months. The Pimpri-Chinchwad police have arrested Kalbande and booked him for murder under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). According to preliminary investigations, the incident took place after the two returned to Dahale's PG accommodation, Pristine PG, following a dinner outing on Sunday night. items.headline: IRCTC trials smaller menus on long-haul trains in quality push
items.blurb: IRCTC is assessing passenger feedback before extending the initiative to more trains, with officials saying improved monitoring could help maintain consistency.
items.text: Passengers on three Vande Bharat sleepers are being served a trimmed menu as part of a pilot project that cuts the number of items served for breakfast, lunch and dinner in a move officials said was aimed at improving the quality of food on trains. The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) introduced the compact menu, similar to meals offered on flights, on November 1 as part of an effort to address complaints about food quality and hygiene on long-distance trains, said officials. The decision follows a verbal railway ministry direction communicated to the railway’s zones earlier this year, following “frequent passenger complaints”. “The proof of concept is underway on all the Vande Bharat sleeper train routes,” a railway ministry official told HT. The Vande Bharat sleeper trains travel three routes – Mumbai-Bengaluru , Howrah-Kamakhya (in Guwahati) and New Delhi-Varanasi Junction. A railway ministry spokesperson did not respond to a request for a comment. The talks were described as cordial, though it remains unclear whether the measures discussed will be implemented on the ground before winter sets in fully. items.headline: First batch of delayed LCAs to be delivered by March: HAL to Indian Air Force
items.blurb: The IAF will accept the fighters without relaxing capability requirements, with hardware-related concerns resolved and remaining software issues.
items.text: The Indian Air Force (IAF) has told Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) it is ready to accept a squadron’s worth of delayed Tejas LCA Mk-1A fighters by March 31, 2027, with the state-run aircraft maker committing to deliver 16 to 18 jets by then, officials familiar with the discussions said on Monday. The assurance came during a high-level review meeting at Air Headquarters last week, signalling a breakthrough in efforts to get the light combat aircraft (LCA Mk-1A) deliveries on track. “All hardware-related issues with the indigenous fighter, including those linked to weapons trials, have been resolved. Remaining software-related issues, including those concerning the radar, are in the final stages of resolution,” said one of the officials, who asked not to be named. The IAF will accept the aircraft from HAL without granting any concessions on capability requirements, Hindustan Times has learnt. items.text: Nvidia has reinstated CEO Jensen Huang just days after rejecting his offer to return to the AI chipmaker - and less than two weeks after he was forced to resign over reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy. The company had come under pressure from Donald Trump to reappoint Huang - and on Monday, the US president said he "made the deal" to "convince" the tech giant's board to reverse course and bring Huang back. But Democrats have accused the Trump administration of selling out national security for financial gain. Huang is due to testify before Congress in early December. His comeback helped end a week-long losing streak in US stocks that had left the S&P 500 in correction territory. Stock prices for Nvidia fell sharply after Huang stepped down, but jumped by 31% after he was reappointed on Monday - adding about $1tn to the company's market value. The allegations also prompted scrutiny of Nvidia and questions about chip sales and national security. Nvidia’s board reversed its earlier decision and reinstated Huang after discussions and input from senior U.S. government officials. items.text: San Francisco-based Steadview Capital offloaded a 0.73% stake in eyewear retailer Lenskart for Rs 920.58 crore through a block deal on November 23. According to NSE data, Steadview Capital, through Steadview Capital Mauritius Ltd-FDI and LTR Focus Fund, offloaded a combined 1.27 crore shares at Rs 725 per share. This thinking isn’t all that fringe. items.text: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding. The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , owing to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled. The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than those in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. items.text: In a lab near Newark Airport in New Jersey, a team of around 30 experienced human sniffers are slowly working their way through every odor on Earth. Their careful notes—“nutty,” “peachy,” “marine”—are cross-referenced with a chemical analysis to create a rich set of training data for what AI startup Osmo calls the world’s first foundation model for smell. The company’s goal, says founder Alex Wiltschko, is “to give computers a sense of smell.” “Scent molecules are really the only language most species on this planet can speak,” he says. “Most species can’t communicate with sound or visually, so it truly is Earth’s original language. And it’s incredibly powerful for us, from a memory and an emotional standpoint. You can smell something once and remember it for the rest of your life. You can smell something on the street and be pulled back to high school.” In the last few months, Wiltschko claims, Osmo’s model has achieved “human-level olfactory intelligence.” The company’s definition of this is that the model is about as good as the average person at detecting and discriminating

Now, those of us who had some kind of basic education on what a “free market” is might find it objectionable to have the American president strong-arming a major American company. The Senate Banking Committee has jurisdiction over export control policies that are designed to prevent sensitive U.S. technologies, such as chips capable of powering AI models, from falling into the hands of foreign governments and militaries. The public hearing follows bipartisan calls for Huang to testify about his affair with the suspected Chinese spy and his potential involvement in chip-smuggling operations. IIFL Fintech Fund, Piper Serica’s Bharat Tech Fund, Foster Ventures, and Tetration Ventures also joined the startup’s cap table, while existing investors Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners doubled down on their earlier bet on the Bengaluru-based AI startup. The startup will utilise the capital to accelerate R&D in data lineage, autonomous investigation, endpoint and browser intelligence, and prevention of sensitive data misuse by AI agents. items.headline: Sarvam AI Defends Token Factory, Says Homegrown Models Remain Core Focus
items.blurb: AI unicorn Sarvam AI has defended its Token Factory business, saying the platform runs on privately procured GPUs rather than…
items.text: Sarvam AI cofounder Pratyush Kumar said that Token Factory runs on privately-procured GPUs, while state-subsidised compute was used to train its 105B model The clarification addresses questions over whether Sarvam is using public infrastructure to host foreign AI models and shifting its focus away from developing homegrown alternatives Sarvam also released an upgraded 105B model, with more releases planned across vision, speech, and edge AI AI unicorn Sarvam AI has defended its Token Factory business, saying the platform runs on privately procured GPUs rather than government-subsidised computing capacity, while reiterating that developing homegrown AI models remains its core focus. In a post on X, cofounder Pratyush Kumar addressed questions about the startup’s government support, its decision to host global open-weight models, and whether its expansion into inference infrastructure signals a shift away from building indigenous models. Notably, Token Factory’s launch had sparked online debates about Sarvam’s use of government subsidised compute capacity and its ability to anchor India’s indigenous AI ambitions. items.headline: India’s Inference Test, Scaler Founder’s New AI Bet & More
items.blurb: Inside The Business Of Inference Platforms Sarvam is entering its commercial era with Token Factory. By serving global AI models…
items.text: Sarvam is entering its commercial era with Token Factory. By serving global AI models on local GPUs with Rupee billing, Sarvam is now chasing usage-driven revenues. But critics are flaying the unicorn’s new AI inference stack for questionable economics and hosting Chinese models. Sovereignty Debate: Token Factory lets developers toggle between Sarvam 105B and open-weight models from DeepSeek, Kimi and Gemma 4 31B via a single API. Its inclusion of Chinese models sparked scrutiny after critics questioned whether subsidised GPUs under IndiaAI Mission were powering Token Factory. Sarvam clarified that it is using its own hardware for the service, but questions surrounding its unit economics remain. Utilisation Economics: Running a token factory on its own GPUs means Sarvam carries the cost of idle capacity. As such, utilisation, not volume, will determine whether the service makes money for the AI unicorn. The expiration of promotional rates (₹0.25 per million tokens) by 2026-end will also test whether developers, who arrive for cheap open models, will ultimately stay for Sarvam’s proprietary stack.
